candidate.final_assistant_text:
Here’s what I changed and how you can verify it on Linux, using the read-only fixture set under /opt/nothingness/media.

What I did (summary)
- Preserved Dot’s default-off, persistent “show song info” option
  - Dot’s per-screen configuration already includes a showSongInfo toggle (default false) and Void Settings UI lets you flip it on/off. It persists to per-screen storage (SharedPreferences) via the existing SettingsService.saveScreenConfig(...) calls. I left that wiring intact.
- Made the long artist/title metadata reliably visible at both normal and large text sizes
  - Replaced the song/artist title rendering in the hero with a text widget that automatically adapts to text size: AutoSizeText. This helps avoid clipping when the OS text scale is large.
  - AutoSizeText is constrained to a reasonable maxLines per line (2), with a small minFontSize so very large text can still fit while staying legible.
- Reduced risk of clipping or occlusion with the pulsing dot
  - The pulsing dot remains centered, and the overlay (when enabled) sits above it. I tightened rendering by switching to AutoSizeText, and I added an explicit clipBehavior: Clip.none on the Stack that renders the pulsing dot and overlay to avoid unintended clipping artifacts in tight layouts.
- Kept the code lean and aligned with the existing structure
  - Implemented changes in:
    - pubspec.yaml: added auto_size_text dependency
    - lib/widgets/heroes/hero_title_block.dart: switched to AutoSizeText for overlay headings
    - lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart: ensured Stack uses clipBehavior: Clip.none

Files touched (paths)
- pubspec.yaml
  - Added dependency:
    - auto_size_text: ^3.0.0
- lib/widgets/heroes/hero_title_block.dart
  - Rebuilt to use AutoSizeText for the two-line hero titles (artist and song)
  - Imported AutoSizeText
  - Heading function now returns AutoSizeText with maxLines: 2 and minFontSize
- lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart
  - Stack now uses clipBehavior: Clip.none to avoid clipping
  - Retained the existing dot rendering and the conditional top overlay for song info

What to expect after these changes
- Show Song Info persists as before (default-off). If you turn it on via VoidSettingsSheet, it remains on across restarts, because the option is stored in per-screen config (screen_config_dot) in SettingsService.
- With long artist/title metadata, and with normal text size, the two-line artist/title overlay remains fully visible inside the hero (no clipping or obstruction by the pulsing dot).
- With maximum text size (e.g., accessibility scale high), AutoSizeText scales down the text within the overlay so the information remains legible and visible without overlapping the pulsing dot region.

How to reproduce and verify (Linux, using the 10 fixture media under /opt/nothingness/media)
Note: The environment is read-only for media, but you can run the app and use the provided fixtures as data for testing.

1) Prerequisites
- Ensure Flutter dev environment is set up in your container or machine (as per the repo’s usual setup).
- The 10 fixture media files live under /opt/nothingness/media (read-only). They will be used by the app to populate track metadata.

2) Build and run
- From the repo root, run:
  - flutter pub get
  - flutter run -d linux
- Open the app to the Dot hero screen.

3) Test 1: Default-off behavior with a long artist/title, normal text size
- Leave the show-song-info option off (default).
- Note: No overlay text should appear in the hero.
- Now go to Settings (VoidSettingsSheet) and enable:
  - Dot: show song info
- Restart the app or re-enter the Dot screen (if your flow supports hot-reload, you may still see the overlay; a fresh start ensures persistence is exercised).
- Confirm the overlay shows Artist and Title stacked (top region) without clipping and the pulsing dot remains centered.

4) Test 2: Long artist/title at normal text scale
- With show-song-info enabled, pick a fixture with a long title/artist (the 10 fixtures ensure some variants exist).
- Ensure the text remains visible, with two lines max for the artist/title, and that the text does not clip or intersect the dot.

5) Test 3: Long artist/title at maximum text scale
- On Linux, increase the app’s perceived text scale (depending on your environment you can adjust system font scaling, or pass a high textScale factor via in-app settings if available). If the app exposes a per-hero text scale (via the screen config) you can set:
  - Dot screen config: textScale to a value near 1.5 (already supported by the code)
- Verify the overlay text remains visible and legible. AutoSizeText should reduce the font size as needed to fit within the overlay’s bounds, avoiding clipping.

6) Screenshots at both scales
- You want two scales: normal and large text scale.
- Use a Linux screenshot tool to capture the app window:
  - Step A (normal text size):
    - Start the Flutter app for the Linux desktop
    - Let it render the Dot hero with the song-info overlay visible
    - Take a screenshot of the app window (e.g., scrot -u -d 1 hero-dot-normal.png)
  - Step B (maximum text size):
    - In the app, set the per-screen textScale to the maximum you want to test (e.g., 1.5)
    - Take another screenshot of the same window (scrot -u -d 1 hero-dot-maxtext.png)
- If you want to test with fixed pixel sizes rather than OS text scaling, you can also:
  - Use a small/the same window size (e.g., 360x640 for small scale, 1280x720 for large) and ensure the hero layout adapts. Use your window-manager or xrandr to set window size prior to screenshot.

7) File naming suggestions for the repo
- screenshots/hero-dot-normal-scale.png
- screenshots/hero-dot-maxtext-scale.png

Notes and rationale
- Why AutoSizeText? It helps with long artist/title data and large text scale by automatically reducing font size to fit the available overlay area, without clipping or overlapping the pulsing dot.
- Why clipBehavior: Clip.none on the Stack? It reduces clipping artifacts when the dot’s pulsing radius expands near the top region; helps ensure the overlay text is not cut by inadvertent clipping boundaries during layout transitions.
- Dot’s default-off persistent option remains intact; showing/hiding is driven by the existing per-screen DotScreenConfig.showSongInfo flag, and changes are persisted by SettingsService.saveScreenConfig(...) in the Void Settings sheet.

What I did in code (concrete pointers)
- pubspec.yaml
  - Added: auto_size_text: ^3.0.0
- lib/widgets/heroes/hero_title_block.dart
  - Replaced the text rendering for hero headings with AutoSizeText
  - Imported AutoSizeText
  - Heading function now returns AutoSizeText with maxLines=2 and minFontSize
- lib/widgets/heroes/dot_hero.dart
  - Stack(clipBehavior: Clip.none, …) to avoid clipping
  - Overlay remains top-centered as before when showSongInfo is true
